question: For real-speaker Japanese dialogue continuations, what incremental changes in generative behaviour arise when a small language model receives an abstract style profile (S), participant-authored persona statements (F), and prior dialogue (H), separately and jointly?
claim_boundary: The pilot estimates conditioning-package effects in eight development speakers; it is not independent validation.
S is an automatic surface/stylometric description, not validated human Persona Fidelity.
F consists of participant-authored persona statements whose temporal truth is unknown; it is not a verified fact database.
Natural H contains both surface and content cues. Effects are incremental prompt-package effects, not pure orthogonal psychological constructs.
A single held-out human continuation is one observed response, not the unique correct response.
No confirmatory significance test is registered.

data.candidate_cohort: the frozen 76-speaker development style-signal cohort only
data.split_enforcement_scan: All 233 speaker IDs and every dialogue participant header are scanned to enforce the frozen split.
data.privacy: Participant text, identifiers, prompts, references, and row-level generations remain under ignored .local paths. Public evidence contains only code, hashes, and aggregates.

blocks.allocation: first four deterministically selected speakers x C0-C7 = 32 requests
remaining four deterministically selected speakers x C0-C7 = 32 requests

allocation.within_case_order: For within-case ordinal p=0..7, execute condition index p XOR the case's fixed mask. Across eight speakers each condition occupies every ordinal once; within each four-speaker block S, F, and H are each 2/2 at every ordinal.
allocation.block_rule: B2 is not contingent on observed response quality. It may stop only for a predeclared safety, integrity, technical, time, or cumulative-budget failure.
allocation.dependence: Eight conditions are paired within each speaker-context; model responses are not treated as 64 independent subjects.

selection.speaker_rule: Within the frozen 76-speaker cohort, retain speakers satisfying all chronology, separation, no-mask, Japanese-text, and leakage rules; rank by SHA-256 of the fixed selection seed plus speaker ID; take the first eight.
selection.style_source: Two earlier dialogues with distinct partners, each partner distinct from the target partner; at least 20 total speaker turns.
selection.target: A later distinct-partner dialogue with parseable nondecreasing timestamps and an eligible target-speaker response immediately after a partner query.
selection.history: The six real turns immediately before the fixed current partner query.
selection.reference: The next real target-speaker turn; never included in any prompt.
selection.unknown_timestamps: Any dialogue with an empty, invalid, or NaT timestamp is ineligible.
selection.leakage_rule: After NFKC, casefold, and whitespace removal, reject exact reference containment and any conditioning string sharing a contiguous substring at least 80% of normalized reference length. Additionally reject F/reference overlap of four contiguous normalized characters, any shared Han bigram, any shared Katakana trigram, or any shared Latin/digit run of length at least three. This is conservative lexical protection, not proof against semantic paraphrase leakage.

factors.S: A numeric Japanese-language description of seven surface/stylometric descriptors (mean and SD of turn length plus five rates) derived only from the two earlier source dialogues; no raw source utterance is supplied.
factors.F: A bulleted list of the speaker's ten participant-authored persona statements; temporal truth unknown.
factors.H: Six chronological raw turns preceding the fixed current partner query in the later target dialogue.
factors.format_control: Every condition has the same system instruction and the same four Japanese section headers. Disabled S/F/H sections are empty, never populated with literal N/A placeholders. The current partner query is identical across all eight conditions for a case.

automatic_applicable_to_all.name: structural_response_validity
automatic_applicable_to_all.meaning: nonempty natural-language response without an exposed prompt label or native API failure

automatic_applicable_to_all.name: Japanese_script_rate
automatic_applicable_to_all.meaning: Japanese-script characters divided by non-space characters
automatic_applicable_to_all.claim_limit: language compatibility proxy, not response quality

automatic_applicable_to_all.name: heldout_reference_character_ngram_F1
automatic_applicable_to_all.meaning: surface resemblance to the single real continuation
automatic_applicable_to_all.formula: NFKC, casefold, remove whitespace, retain punctuation; form SETS of character trigrams and compute harmonic F1. A successful empty or fewer-than-three-character generation scores 0; every reference has at least eight characters.
automatic_applicable_to_all.claim_limit: not correctness and not Persona Fidelity

automatic_applicable_to_all.name: source_style_surface_distance
automatic_applicable_to_all.meaning: equal-weight mean absolute distance, lower is closer, on six response-observable coordinates: mean response length divided by 50, and question, exclamation, ellipsis, laughter, and polite-ending rates on 0..1 scales
automatic_applicable_to_all.formula: Compute the six coordinates with the frozen style parser for the generated reply and the two-dialogue source profile; average the six absolute coordinate differences. Source SD may appear descriptively in S but is excluded because one reply has no within-output turn SD.
automatic_applicable_to_all.claim_limit: exploratory proxy whose validity controls must be reported; short outputs may be unstable

automatic_applicable_to_all.name: conditioning_copy_rate
automatic_applicable_to_all.meaning: exact and character-ngram reuse from S, F, H, and query fields
automatic_applicable_to_all.formula: For every output, compare separately with each case's latent S, F, H, and query text regardless of whether that factor was exposed. Under the same NFKC/casefold/whitespace normalization, report (a) precision of the SET of unique generated character trigrams found in the source and (b) longest-common-substring length divided by normalized generated length. Empty or fewer-than-three-character generation has trigram precision 0; empty generation has LCS ratio 0.
automatic_applicable_to_all.claim_limit: diagnoses copying; copying is not persona success

outcomes.missingness: Keep every request. A native/API failure has structural validity 0 and all text-derived outcomes missing. A successful empty response has structural validity 0, reference-F1 and copy metrics 0, Japanese-script rate and style distance missing, and length 0. Nonempty short replies follow each frozen formula. Report numerator/denominator coverage for every outcome. Never score a non-applicable semantic endpoint as zero.

estimands.coding: For each speaker use x_S=2S-1, x_F=2F-1, and x_H=2H-1. For any nonempty factor subset A, its Hadamard effect is 2 times the mean across eight conditions of y multiplied by the product of x_j for j in A. Thus a main effect is mean(y|factor=1)-mean(y|factor=0); interactions use the same product coding.
estimands.primary_developmental: Within-speaker Hadamard main effects of S, F, and H on each applicable outcome, followed by the mean across eight speaker units.
estimands.secondary: Within-speaker SF, SH, FH, and SFH product-coded interactions; condition means; copy-rate changes; CPU latency and memory differences.
estimands.uncertainty: Report eight speaker-level contrast values, their mean, median, range, and leave-one-speaker-out mean range. These are descriptive/influence summaries, not confidence intervals or calibrated confirmatory tests.
estimands.human_estimands: Remain NOT_OBSERVED until genuine blinded judgments are collected under a separately frozen provenance protocol.

required_before_inference: all native prompt token counts plus maximum-new-token fit
valid automatic scorer implementation and tests
frozen formulas, normalizers, missingness handling, and factorial contrast implementation matching this design
required_before_semantic_analysis_or_cla: a separately frozen condition-blinded genuine-human review protocol; this is not a prerequisite for the automatic-proxy generations
